*Naomi pauses, registering the answer. For once there's no argument over the chain of control.*
*Venn permits herself half a breath of amusement after the channel closes. The convoy resumes, smaller in cargo, intact in passengers, with Thunderbreak's port-bow scrape plainly visible.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: It's bigger than the pictures.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: The pictures didn't have the line.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: Maybe we're in the wrong line.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: We've tried three. This is the one for people who want beds.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Three taken. One split after the cutter disconnected. Everyone who boarded at Luminara is here.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Good. Excellent. The dead would have made an ugly accounting problem.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: That came out wrong. I'm glad they're alive. I'm also thinking about traders who paid for grain they won't receive. Both are true.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Have the inspectors count what's physically docked. No promises based on what was loaded at Luminara.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: And before the wholesalers start calling it a Fleet loss, remind them it is Verge grain.

panelPlan: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT
The boy looks up so far his mother has to tug his sleeve to keep him moving.
Naomi gives him a look. Wallace regrets the words immediately.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT*

*Auric is spectacular. Its rings and civilized concourses have the confident beauty of a place prosperous enough to build public space for pleasure. Under that architecture, people are standing in lines with luggage, waiting for heat and a place to sleep. The Luminara freighter docks. All its passengers disembark alive.*
*The boy looks up so far his mother has to tug his sleeve to keep him moving.*

*Dock staff count remaining grain while laborers separate three empty container positions from one visibly ruptured unit. Naomi is standing with Venn at the manifest desk when Halev and Wallace arrive from the civic freight office.*
*Naomi gives him a look. Wallace regrets the words immediately.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Nobody aboard Thunderbreak is claiming ownership. Our damage record will follow the manifest.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I was going to say exactly that, but less elegantly.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I suspect you still might.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Depends what you do next.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: How long have they been standing here?

dialogueInline.speaker: CIVIC WORKER
dialogueInline.text: New arrivals? About an hour. Housing asked us to send everyone to the same desk. They haven't sent a desk clerk.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then send someone from my office.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: They are already doing freight compensation.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: They can spend the next hour doing this. It will probably be the better use of their time.

panelPlan: Halev's attention has moved to a registration queue near a heater. An older resident is sharing the warmest spot with a new arrival; both have coat collars.
Halev walks to the mother, not with a practiced speech but because she is next in the line.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Halev's attention has moved to a registration queue near a heater. An older resident is sharing the warmest spot with a new arrival; both have coat collars turned up. The mother and boy wait a few paces behind.*
*Halev walks to the mother, not with a practiced speech but because she is next in the line.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: You've got a berth assignment?

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: I've got three pieces of paper and a son who has been promised the best rooms in Auric.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: I didn't say best.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: Better. A very specific word.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We have places to register tonight. I can't promise every room is ready.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: We came because we'd heard there was work, and heat, and somewhere to live. I can wait for work. It's the other two I worry about.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Open the civic warming room. Seat families there until housing can make an actual plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Some of those rooms are booked tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Tomorrow the booking office can bring its complaint to me. Tonight the rooms are warm.

panelPlan: Halev looks toward the beautiful concourse, then at the unused area beyond a civilian meeting room.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Halev looks toward the beautiful concourse, then at the unused area beyond a civilian meeting room.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — EVENING INTO NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: I'll put that in writing before the office does it for me.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: Are the rooms really warmer?

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: The room you're going to tonight is. I haven't seen the one you'll have next week.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: That's what my mother said.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then she's ahead of the government.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The markets at both ends will feel this loss. A permanent fast route could make it up in weeks. If traders still trust it.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: People will come faster, too.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: That's how a successful port usually works.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then we should find out what kind of port we can afford to be.

panelPlan: The boy looks up at the governor after the group begins to disperse.
As registration resumes, Wallace walks beside Halev.
They leave under lights beautiful enough to conceal the cold only from someone who hasn't been standing in it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The boy looks up at the governor after the group begins to disperse.*
*The mother almost laughs. Her hand is still tight around the bag. Halev notices but doesn't remark on it.*
*As registration resumes, Wallace walks beside Halev.*
*They leave under lights beautiful enough to conceal the cold only from someone who hasn't been standing in it.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: That's not my chair.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I know. Yours looks uncomfortable.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: It's the only reason anyone leaves.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: That and the prices.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I gave you a crossing time. I didn't promise the freighter would come back in pieces.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It came back in one piece. An important piece is missing a few expensive things, but that's a different complaint.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Three stolen containers. A fourth torn open. Two merchants are already delaying their next departures.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Venn put a wreck across our approach. We took the three intact. Do you want me to apologize for not stealing the broken one?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'd like you to recognize that merchants don't enjoy having their ships disassembled.

panelPlan: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT
Billie Rusk arrives without waiting to be welcomed. Her bright hair and Shard flightwear are unmistakable. She helps herself to a chair that belongs.
She eyes the token. Jex covers it with a hand.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT*

*Jex Marrin occupies the edge of a busy trade passage, where people negotiate freight beside food stalls that are closing for the night. He has a small physical route token under his thumb and a merchant's angry message in front of him. He reads it twice, not because the words are unclear, but because he is considering how not to answer them.*
*Billie Rusk arrives without waiting to be welcomed. Her bright hair and Shard flightwear are unmistakable. She helps herself to a chair that belongs to the neighboring table and tips it toward Jex.*
*She eyes the token. Jex covers it with a hand.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Neither do I. Tess is probably going to make me spend an entire shift fixing Ashfang's collar. I'll send you the bill.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You can send it. My waste chute accepts almost anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: We brought food home. The families at Black Drift can eat tonight. When was the last time your merchants lost sleep because a Shard household had an empty table?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Last night, I suspect. They're frightened enough to avoid the crossing, and they were just starting to trust it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Trust Fleet, you mean.

panelPlan: Billie smiles. It's an old exchange. Her smile fades when he brings up the traders again.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Billie smiles. It's an old exchange. Her smile fades when he brings up the traders again.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Trust the route. Very different thing, and I'd like to keep them different. If the merchant ships stop coming, you won't have grain to take, and I won't have grain to negotiate over. There's a little tragedy for both our professions.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You want us dependent on the next shipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I want there to be a next shipment. After that I expect to fight with you about it, possibly over a nicer table.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You keep talking as if you get to make the plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I have persuaded more than one captain to listen to a plan.

panelPlan: Billie watches two workers carry a ruined freight strap toward repair.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Billie watches two workers carry a ruined freight strap toward repair.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You persuaded me to listen to a crossing time. And I listened. Don't start confusing favors with the wheel of my ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: No, I suppose that would be dangerous.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It already is. But you're still going to give me the next one, aren't you?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The next what?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You do like testing people.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: No, Jex. I like knowing them.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Tell the merchants we left their passengers alone.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I will. They may even find that comforting.

panelPlan: Jex turns the token over in his palm.
For a moment the two are quiet. Then Billie puts the borrowed chair back exactly where she found it, to Jex's surprise.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Jex turns the token over in his palm.*
*For a moment the two are quiet. Then Billie puts the borrowed chair back exactly where she found it, to Jex's surprise.*

settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — DOCK-SIDE BROKER TABLE, LATE NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They should. It was a choice.

panelPlan: She goes. Jex begins writing a reply to the merchant. He erases his first sentence. A second message arrives before he's found a better one.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *She goes. Jex begins writing a reply to the merchant. He erases his first sentence. A second message arrives before he's found a better one.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Well, that's worse than it looked when it was on fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It wasn't on fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then your crew should stop describing it that way. Makes the repairs sound more exciting than they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Can you patch it?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Can you stop hitting things with it?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I'll take that as a yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: The families want the last container opened now. The collar crew wants the lift under the pressure frame. I have one lift and two people who both think I'm doing my job badly.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Are they wrong?

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

panelPlan: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY
Tessa Banks, sleeves rolled above a repaired flightwear underlayer, presses a tool against an ugly stretch of the collar frame. The tool gives a.
Abby arrives from the ration point. She has been carrying a crate herself. A worker hurries toward her before she can set it down.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY*

*The captured containers have arrived intact. Workers distribute grain into household allotments while welders inspect the damaged cargo collar of Ashfang Marauder. Families wait with crates and handcarts, neither grateful supplicants nor a faceless crowd. Everyone has something else to do after they collect the food.*
*Tessa Banks, sleeves rolled above a repaired flightwear underlayer, presses a tool against an ugly stretch of the collar frame. The tool gives a noise she clearly dislikes.*
*Abby arrives from the ration point. She has been carrying a crate herself. A worker hurries toward her before she can set it down.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then you're having a better morning than I am. Use the lift for the grain while the weld cools. Brace the pressure frame where it is. Tess signs it off before we load it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: And if somebody tries to hurry me, they can explain to Billie why her next docking collar will be made of optimism.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I prefer metal.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You can tell me that when you stop scraping it off on other ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Three containers past a Fleet cruiser. That counts for something.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: It does.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: That's not how you say it when you're pleased.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I am pleased. I'm also looking at how long it has to last.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: People are eating tonight.

panelPlan: The worker gets the lift moving. Billie watches a parent divide a small grain allotment into two bags and give one to an older neighbor.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The worker gets the lift moving. Billie watches a parent divide a small grain allotment into two bags and give one to an older neighbor.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: And two traders delayed their next runs. People will need to eat next week.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: There'll be another crossing.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Assuming we finish the collar before our next birthdays.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You spend more time insulting it than fixing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: It's a very old collar. It needs encouragement.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You're doing it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Doing what?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Turning dinner into an examination.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Two traders just pushed their crossings back. I don't like the pattern.

panelPlan: Much later, the three share a small meal on an overturned work crate just beyond the repair bay. Tess keeps a seal brace in her lap. Billie is hungry enough to.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Much later, the three share a small meal on an overturned work crate just beyond the repair bay. Tess keeps a seal brace in her lap. Billie is hungry enough to eat before sitting down. Abby is reviewing the delayed merchant departures.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I don't like that they can decide when we eat.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Neither do the traders. They'd rather have us buy the food and leave their ships alone. A sentimental lot.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: What if the food came here without us intercepting it?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You mean buy it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Buy some. Trade what we can. Arrange delivery. Something that leaves the ships in one piece.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: And ask Fleet's permission to use the road while we do it?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They don't own the whole road.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They act like they do. They'll send one cruiser today, three tomorrow. Then we'll be paying to pass the place where our people used to live.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: If every crossing ends with wreckage, there won't be a road worth taking.

panelPlan: Billie stops chewing.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Billie stops chewing.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It's easy to talk about stopping raids when you've got food on your plate.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I went hungry with you. Don't make me prove it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I didn't mean—

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I know. But you said it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Would one of you hold this before I decide it's personally offended me?

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You really think merchants will sail here willingly?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I think we ought to find out before there aren't any left.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Suppose they're willing only because Fleet's got guns on them.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then it's not what I'm asking for.

panelPlan: The words land harder than Billie expected. The food came from the very raid they're discussing. Abby doesn't answer immediately.
Tess slides the brace into the space between them with a decisive clack.
Abby takes one end. Billie takes the other. The familiar division of work returns without solving anything.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The words land harder than Billie expected. The food came from the very raid they're discussing. Abby doesn't answer immediately.*
*Tess slides the brace into the space between them with a decisive clack.*
*Abby takes one end. Billie takes the other. The familiar division of work returns without solving anything.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — WORKING SHARD REPAIR YARD, THEN ASHFANG'S BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You two can invent a new civilization when I get this frame shut. Right now, lift.

panelPlan: They lift together. A waiting family passes beyond the repair rail with an allotment that will feed them for a little while. Ashfang's collar remains partly.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: The standing grain order remains. Cutters take what the frontier carries.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: At the last crossing, they also damaged the vehicle carrying it.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: One convoy. Three containers reached our people.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Two merchants have suspended their departures. If the next two do the same, what exactly will our cutters take?

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR
dialogueInline.text: The Core will keep sending guards. It has to. It calls that obligation a virtue. I call it an expense.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: The expense doesn't fall on one side. We have grain today and fewer ships willing to come tomorrow.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: You're responsible for getting the next shipment home intact.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can plan an interception. I can't repair a merchant's confidence with a weapon.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR
dialogueInline.text: Confidence is an easily changed feeling.

panelPlan: BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER
Three political authorities occupy their distinct established places, each masked differently. The chamber has worn flooring and practical working tables; no.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER*

*Three political authorities occupy their distinct established places, each masked differently. The chamber has worn flooring and practical working tables; no ceremony suggests magic. Abby stands where petitioning captains stand, a tablet of actual shipping losses in her hand. Captains are politically accountable but independently command their own ships.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: So is fear. Neither puts grain on a table without a ship delivering it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: What do you propose?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Stop treating the freighter as a disposable container. The ship is what brings the next cargo. If you want supplies, you need people willing to send them.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: Your captains already know how to take cargo without breaking ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Billie's cutter took an unsound approach because Fleet moved the wreck. It can happen again. There are limits to what the crew can control.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: Then they should learn to manage the limits.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR
dialogueInline.text: A visible risk can be useful. The Core should not be allowed to believe protection is free.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Nor should merchants be allowed to believe this market is dead.

panelPlan: The Trade Mask turns toward Abby, attentive. Raid does not.
The three masks are not speaking for one mind. Abby sees that and takes the opening without overstating it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The Trade Mask turns toward Abby, attentive. Raid does not.*
*The three masks are not speaking for one mind. Abby sees that and takes the opening without overstating it.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SILENT TRIARCH CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Then let us keep the crossings usable. I'll bring you food where I can. But if a ship breaks, calling it a lesson won't fill the holds.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: The order is unchanged.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

panelPlan: Trade studies her. Raid makes no concession. Fear looks toward the visible tally of crossings that have been deferred.
She leaves without pretending she has won. Behind her, the three authorities continue disagreeing about what the same shortage means.

summary: THE COST OF GETTING WHAT YOU WANT (RF_I01_P14–P15) — 1/4
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC ROUTE OFFICE — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC ROUTE OFFICE — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The growers think regular fast crossings could make last night's loss back in weeks. That's not an exaggeration. We can finally put perishable goods on the other side before they become fertilizer.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Assuming the markers hold and nobody treats the slow approach like the fast segment.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: You're constitutionally unable to be happy about good news.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I like good news. I simply prefer it after the measurements.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: How many new arrivals can we house if regular runs begin?

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: That's a separate budget.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Unfortunately, the arrivals won't separate themselves by budget.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: More freight means more work. More work helps us build housing.

summary: THE COST OF GETTING WHAT YOU WANT (RF_I01_P14–P15) — 2/4
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC ROUTE OFFICE — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Eventually. The boy who came from Luminara wanted to know where he'd sleep last night. We gave him a public room. That's what we actually have today.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We can't refuse trade because someone is cold.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Nor can we declare trade a success because someone can afford a warmer room when it arrives.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: There's another question. Fleet wants a standing escort assignment. If they maintain the high-speed markers, they'll have a legitimate operational stake in what happens on the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: We need their cruisers.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I know. I was on the other end of the approach yesterday. I just don't need them deciding which Verge freighter gets to dock first.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceScene: SCENE 10 — THE COST OF GETTING WHAT YOU WANT (RF_I01_P14–P15)

summary: THE COST OF GETTING WHAT YOU WANT (RF_I01_P14–P15) — 3/4
settingText: AURIC BAZAAR — CIVIC ROUTE OFFICE — NEXT MORNING

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We'll propose separate responsibilities. Fleet maintains and verifies what it can measure; Fleet commands its own patrol ships. Verge pilots control the slow approaches. Civilian ports keep cargo and crossing order.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Dominion will ask for a lasting commitment.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Of course he will. If I were building routes for a living, I'd ask for it too.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then put the expiry and review on the page. Don't make a one-way obligation because we're relieved someone brought the repair tools.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: I'll support it. I just want it understood that every day of delay is another day we pay the old price of distance.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Put that in the council report. Alongside the heat allotment.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The council will hate that.

panelPlan: Halev starts revising the conditions. Wallace stays, because he sees the opportunity more clearly than he dislikes the burden.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I know. Let's give them two things they need to read.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: And make sure the escort agreement is written before any captain mistakes a favor for a jurisdiction.

settingText: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: That's a serious-looking abrasion for a ship that wasn't meant to touch anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It is mostly an insult to the paintwork. The structural inspection is less offended.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: You say that now. The yard will want an entire week to explain how offended it is.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: The maneuver kept a cutter off the freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: One cutter. The other boarded. Three containers were taken, and a different one was lost when the fitting split. The civilian passengers arrived alive.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Good. Tell us about the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: The reblazed segment holds verification. Verge pilots have a reliable approach procedure. Auric offers crossing data and joint upkeep, provided port order and civilian freight remain under Verge control.

panelPlan: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER
Dominion and Rhyne occupy a bright, mature Fleet institution. Venn presents the verified Kaldr figures without theatrical flourish. The gouge on.
Venn transfers to the measured reciprocal-field and low-speed exit data.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER*

*Dominion and Rhyne occupy a bright, mature Fleet institution. Venn presents the verified Kaldr figures without theatrical flourish. The gouge on Thunderbreak's port bow is visible in a practical damage projection. Venn doesn't conceal it.*
*Venn transfers to the measured reciprocal-field and low-speed exit data.*

settingText: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: In other words, they want our cruiser but not our opinion.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: They want our opinion about things we understand. They don't need a Fleet officer deciding a local berthing queue.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: We can accept that distinction and still maintain authority over the patrol.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: Today. Tomorrow every trader will assume our ship is there. The day after, the fastest route becomes the only route anyone can afford. Then we aren't offering protection; we're an essential part of their economy.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: That is one of the reasons to restore reliable travel.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: It's also one of the reasons people resent us.

panelPlan: Dominion considers the argument instead of waving it away.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Dominion considers the argument instead of waving it away.*

settingText: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Generations spent planning voyages by how many years they could afford to lose. People abandoned relatives they could not reach. Entire systems developed without knowing whether help was a lifetime away. We are finally able to restore a route that can be maintained. I will not pretend that is a minor responsibility because someone may someday dislike the manner in which we discharge it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Nor should we pretend it's ours merely because we know how to maintain it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I didn't propose annexing Auric, Commodore.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know. I'm asking that the written order make it impossible for an eager lieutenant to think we did.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: At least that costs less than another cruiser.

panelPlan: Dominion looks at her. The disagreement is genuine and not yet adversarial.
Rhyne gives a reluctant, approving nod.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Dominion looks at her. The disagreement is genuine and not yet adversarial.*
*Rhyne gives a reluctant, approving nod.*

settingText: CORE ADMIRALTY — AUTHORIZATION CHAMBER

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You always calculate the cost of being needed. Have you calculated the cost of not being there?

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: Every time we don't have enough ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Trial authorization. Continue the field verification. Patrol the route when Thunderbreak is ready. No local port authority without consent.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Port-bow repairs first.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Naturally.

dialogueInline.speaker: RHYNE
dialogueInline.text: The yard will be delighted. You can have the other half of the discussion when they see what you did to their work.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I was hoping to delegate that part.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You may delegate the paperwork. Not the responsibility.

panelPlan: That, too, is true. Dominion signs a provisional trial authorization, one that requires ongoing verification, beacon maintenance, and available patrol capacity.
Venn accepts the order. She believes in the mission and is alert to its cost. Those facts have not yet come into conflict.

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD ASSEMBLY ORBIT AND DEPARTURE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD ASSEMBLY ORBIT AND DEPARTURE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: The merchants are scheduling again. Gravefire's ready when you two are. Please don't tell me that means we're leaving immediately.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: We could leave immediately.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I see. So you were listening only for an opportunity to be difficult.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: More crossings mean more chances to get food home. Keep the ships intact this time.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: They also mean more Fleet guns. I don't like the idea that our next meal depends on how generously Dominion feels about putting a cruiser in our path.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: It already depends on how the merchants feel about risking their freighters. I'm trying to reduce the number of people whose moods can starve us.

panelPlan: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD ASSEMBLY ORBIT AND DEPARTURE BAY
Ashfang's collar has been repaired enough to fly; the patched history remains visible. Nearby, Gravefire and Scythe of Saville remain separately.
Tess comes out of a work access with a tool in one hand and the look of someone who hasn't slept enough.

*Ashfang's collar has been repaired enough to fly; the patched history remains visible. Nearby, Gravefire and Scythe of Saville remain separately commanded ships. Workers have started securing new provisions and replacement parts. Word of the continued Green Corridor trial has reached the dock.*
*Tess comes out of a work access with a tool in one hand and the look of someone who hasn't slept enough.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD ASSEMBLY ORBIT AND DEPARTURE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Both of you could start by giving back the equipment you keep taking out of my bay.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Borrowing.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Borrowing has a return date. You seem to think it's a matter of archaeological discovery.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's the one I specifically told you not to touch.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I looked after it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You used it to pry something open.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It worked.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: It did. Look at it now.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You think a better arrangement is coming, Abby. I can see it on your face. You think if we behave nicely, someone will decide we deserve to eat.

panelPlan: Billie fishes a small fitting from her pocket, examines it, and hands it back.
Abby laughs, unexpectedly. Billie watches her, then catches it herself. They are still friends. No one has made the later decisions yet.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Billie fishes a small fitting from her pocket, examines it, and hands it back.*
*Abby laughs, unexpectedly. Billie watches her, then catches it herself. They are still friends. No one has made the later decisions yet.*

settingText: BLACK DRIFT — SHARD ASSEMBLY ORBIT AND DEPARTURE BAY

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I think we have to stop measuring success by how much we can take from a ship before it breaks.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: And I think someone ought to pay attention to why we started doing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I would love to live long enough for this argument to become boring. Until then, Ashfang has a flight check and Gravefire needs her own crew back.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You heard her. Ready your ships. Independently, before Billie tries to borrow one of those too.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Yours isn't my type.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Too many working parts?

panelPlan: Neither is prepared to yield that point. Tess tucks the damaged fitting into a pocket.
Billie throws a gloved hand at her. Tess steps easily aside. Work resumes across the bay. Outside, separate Shard vessels prepare for a newly reopened route.
